Action: A1. Fund wheat transformation capability before funding a wheat fixation trait
Go / no-go gate: Genotype-independent transformation at or above 20% efficiency in three commercial cultivars by 2031 (IWGSC, 2018; Debernardi et al., 2020)
Expected consequence: Either wheat becomes able to carry the trait, or the budget moves to the microbial route with no further sunk cost

Action: A2. Verify the microbial route in wheat independently, since it is the only route with wheat evidence
Go / no-go gate: A multi-site trial, not vendor-run, beating +8.9% grain yield and delivering 20 kg N ha⁻¹ or more, with protein reported (Veresoglou & Menexes, 2010; Fox et al., 2016)
Expected consequence: A deployable 20–45 kg N ha⁻¹ input this decade, or an early and cheap negative result
Leading indicator: Measured N delivered and delivered protein, independently run

Action: A3. Specify the trait as baseload nitrogen and keep the tactical late-season window
Go / no-go gate: Design must leave a late window able to move delivered protein by at least one grade step (Bogard et al., 2010; Giordano et al., 2023)
Expected consequence: Growers retain grade control, so the trait is adoptable rather than a price risk
Leading indicator: Share of adopters still reaching their target grade

Action: A4. Launch into feed and domestic grades first, with royalty-free licensing fixed at filing
Go / no-go gate: First release confined to grades with no protein floor, in countries applying under 25 kg N ha⁻¹ (FAO, 2024; Grain Trade Australia, 2025)
Expected consequence: The envelope is sufficient on its own where it is deployed, and the benefit reaches growers who cannot pay for fertiliser
Leading indicator: Hectares adopted in no-floor grades, and licence terms at filing

Action: A5. Correct the accounting before any claim is made
Go / no-go gate: Rate-dependent N₂O factors in Tier 2 inventories, no nonlinearity premium credited to wheat, and the break crop priced separately from nitrogen (Shcherbak et al., 2014; Angus et al., 2015)
Expected consequence: Abatement claims survive audit, and the 0.5 t ha⁻¹ break value is not lost to a nitrogen-only appraisal
Leading indicator: Emission factor basis used, and legume area retained
